title: Built a browser HOI4-lite game with AI coding and me designing. Demo + tech stack
author: thewho7
selftext:
I've been a web dev for 20+ years, but I've never had the time to make a real game on the side - until I heard AI could actually do the coding well now. So I drive the design, the architecture, and every judgment call; the AI does the actual implementation and code. It still took a lot of hours, but in just a few months, I've got a game with a working UI and sims that run pretty well.

It's a lighter, more accessible take on HOI4 for now. Playable alpha, no install, runs in the browser:

https://preview.redd.it/6g4bn4r24j4h1.png?width=1440&format=png&auto=webp&s=98f7ef03da72b85dd60fc3b3ec584d357f543f9f

  \- [https://www.playnationfall.com/demo/](https://www.playnationfall.com/demo/)

  \- Drop straight into WW2 as the USA: [https://www.playnationfall.com/demo/?country=usa&scenario=ww2-1939](https://www.playnationfall.com/demo/?country=usa&scenario=ww2-1939)

You can wage war, run diplomacy, buy real historical military units, manage resources and trade, and watch the AI-run nations fight their own wars around you.

The stack, for the curious:

  \- Vue 3 + Pinia for the app and game state, Vite build. D3/D3 Geo, Electron for future install release, topojson, and world atlas.

  \- Canvas-rendered map - I started on SVG. I hit a wall on mid to late-game frames with thousands of overlay nodes, so the whole map render was migrated to a layered Canvas pipeline (static country fills vs. dynamic overlays, viewport culling, polygon LOD). That took late-game map FPS from \~9 up to smooth and responsive.

  \- A simulation engine that runs the AI nations: combat resolution, diplomacy, coalitions, economy, and trade, all driven by data-defined historical scenarios (WW2 and WW3 for now). Web workers keep the heavy sim work off the main thread.

  \- Inventories climbed past 10k+ units across scenarios, with per-war deterministic RNG channels so sim runs are reproducible, and balance is testable from a CLI (a dev tool just for me, for tuning config values), not just by playing.

On the workflow itself: the wins came from keeping myself on judgment and creativity - what's fun, what's historically correct, what looks cool, what the architecture should be - and pushing everything deterministic and mechanical down to the AI. I've already started a map redo to go more HOI4 in the country detail: rivers, major roads, rail, mountains, and more.

In general, I found that as long as I could keep Claude Code focused, it did pretty well. It was very helpful for historical research, even if I have to keep asking for it to find more country military units, and it finds more and more 😭 It handles Canvas as well as affects on that, even geo stuff very well, which I wasn't expecting.

It's an early alpha and rough in spots. I'd genuinely love feedback - both on whether the game's actually fun, something you'd want to see added, whatever comes to mind. Happy to go deep in the comments - or jump in the Discord: [https://discord.gg/925b78j4us](https://discord.gg/925b78j4us). Thanks!
